The two titles in the old note are one work (the LBL proceedings paper). Table 1 p.8 (PDF p.17) 'Radon and Steam from Production Wells': Larderello (3 plants) 54,000 pCi/L, 3.6 Ci/d, 32,000 t/d; Castelnuovo 141,000, 1.5, 7,300; Sasso 57,000, 0.5, 6,000; Serrazzano 70,000, 1.3, 7,200; Lagoni Rossi 90,000, 0.4, 5,300; Lago 163,000, 0.7, 8,700; Monterotondo 53,000, 0.08, 2,100; total 8.0 Ci/d, 68,600 t/d (verified on page image; S0509 Tab. 3 reproduces it exactly). notes: CORRECTS S1405 (round 3). FULL TEXT READ (PDF supplied by Steve: /mnt/user-data/uploads/radiopassive/import/Interpretation of Radon Concentration in the Serrazzano Zone of the Larderello Geothermal Field.pdf; 7 pp.). short_cite: D'Amore 1975 (Rn-222 survey, Larderello, Part 1; data March-June 1976)
full_citation: D'Amore, F. (1975). Radon-222 survey in Larderello geothermal field, Italy (Part 1). Geothermics 4 (nos 1-4), pp. 96-108. Istituto Internazionale per le Ricerche Geotermiche, CNR, Pisa. notes: CORRECTS S1418 (round 3). FULL TEXT READ (scanned; PDF supplied by Steve: /mnt/user-data/uploads/radiopassive/import/Radon-222 survey in Larderello geothermal field, Italy (Part 1).pdf; 13 pp.). The 'pp. 1-4' in the old note were the issue numbers; printed pages are 96-108. Volume is dated 1975 but the data are from 1976 (survey March-June 1976, references to 1976 in press); year left at 1975 as cited by George 1980 (S1404). PRIMARY DATASET for every Larderello radon figure in the registry. 193 wells, about 200 km2, 1976. Table 1 (pp.102-107, scanned, poorly OCR'd): per well T, P, flow (t/h), gas/steam ratio (Nl/kg), gas % by weight, Rn nCi per L of gas (mostly 1-20) with sigma, Rn nCi per kg of fluid (typically 40-300; well 85 = 162, well 53 = 302) and Rn flux per well (column read as mCi/h: e.g. well 85, 33.0 t/h x 162 nCi/kg = 5.35 vs 5.88 printed). Per-well Rn in the 61 rows I could read cleanly averages about 2.4 mCi/h, so about 10 (range 8-12) Ci/d for 193 wells (my rough extrapolation; not a full transcription), same order as George Table 1 8.0 Ci/d. Condensate carries only a small fraction of the Rn, almost all in the gas phase (p.100, Fig. 5). Highest Rn in shallow wells near recharge zones; central zone about one order of magnitude lower; deepest wells lowest (0.2-2.0 nCi/L gas) (p.105-107). Thoron test (p.102-105, Fabiani well, 24 March 1976): Rn upstream 6.42, 6.30, 6.42 vs downstream 6.67, 6.48, 6.36 nCi/L; no excess upstream, so 'all the radioactivity registered is due to Rn-222': no Rn-220 detected at the wellhead (no detection limit stated). Method accuracy about 10%. Part 2 not located.
